title: Subfield scalar extension preserves local presentations after raw scheme pullback
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\le F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$, let $X,Z$ be schemes, and let $f:Z	o X$ be any morphism. Write $E_W,F_W$ for the pulled-back coefficient rings on a scheme $W$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $G_W=\operatorname{Ext}_{E_W	o F_W}=F_W\otimes_{E_W}-$ for extension along the coefficient inclusion [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For a sheaf of rings $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, let $f^
atural_R=\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$ denote raw pullback of internal modules to modules over $f^{-1}R$ [def-sfb-finite-upper-star, def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal, sk-def-sfb-transport, sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

Let $M$ be an $E_X$-module object. If the $f^{-1}E_X$-module $f^
atural_{E_X}M$ is locally finitely presented [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented], then the $f^{-1}F_X$-module $f^
atural_{F_X}(G_XM)$ is locally finitely presented. More precisely, every pro-étale covering family $\{u_i:U_i	o Z\}$ that witnesses the former local finite presentation also witnesses the latter. There is no restriction on $f$ and no quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ or $Z$.

source.place: Second sentence: tensoring local finite presentations; raw versus coefficient pullback on each stratum and each presentation-cover member (old split steps 2 and 3).

proof.text: Let $\varphi:E_X\to F_X$ be [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]. Put $R=f^{-1}E_X$, $S=f^{-1}F_X$, $\psi=f^{-1}\varphi$, $N=f^\natural_{E_X}M$ and $P=f^\natural_{F_X}(G_XM)$. The ring objects $E_X,F_X$ are commutative: $\underline E,\underline F$ are commutative condensed rings [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring], and pulling back from the point preserves commutativity [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; $\varphi$ is a morphism of ring objects. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-extension-inverse-image] to $f$, $E_X$, $F_X$ and $\varphi$. It supplies an $S$-linear isomorphism $\theta:P\cong S\otimes_R N$. Its statement also supplies the commutative ring objects $R,S$ and their morphism $\psi$; these are the actual inverse-image rings.

source.place: Second sentence, tensoring local finite presentations: first commute scalar extension with the raw pullback to Z.

proof.text:
Fix any covering family $\{u_i:U_i\to Z\}$ witnessing local finite presentation of $N$ in [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. For each $i$, put $R_i=u_i^{-1}R$, $S_i=u_i^{-1}S$, $\psi_i=u_i^{-1}\psi$ and $N_i=u_i^\natural N$. The cover hypothesis says that $N_i$ is finitely presented over $R_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-extension-inverse-image] again, now to $u_i$, $R$, $S$ and $\psi$. Composing its comparison with the image of $\theta$ under the module-transport functor gives an $S_i$-linear isomorphism
\[
u_i^\natural P\cong S_i\otimes_{R_i}N_i.
\]
Here $u_i^\natural$ denotes raw module pullback for the relevant ring. The comparison supplies commutativity of $R_i,S_i$, without identifying them with coefficient rings from a point.

source.place: Second sentence, same local presentation: commute extension with raw pullback to each member of the original presentation cover.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-internal-extension-finite-presentation] on the scheme $U_i$, to the ring morphism $\psi_i:R_i\to S_i$ and the finitely presented $R_i$-module $N_i$. For a presentation $N_i\cong\operatorname{coker}(a_i:R_i^{m_i}\to R_i^{n_i})$, it gives
\[
S_i\otimes_{R_i}N_i\cong\operatorname{coker}(a_{i,S}:S_i^{m_i}\to S_i^{n_i}),
\]
where $a_{i,S}$ is obtained by applying scalar extension to $a_i$ and conjugating by its finite-free isomorphisms. The ranks remain the same finite integers; the lemma assumes no flatness.

source.place: Second sentence, tensoring the local finite-free presentation and retaining its finite ranks.

proof.text: Compose the isomorphisms in steps 2 and 3. They express $u_i^\natural P$ as the cokernel of $a_{i,S}$, so it is finitely presented by [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. This holds for every member of the fixed cover, which therefore witnesses that $P$ is locally finitely presented by [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. The cover was arbitrary among the covers witnessing the hypothesis, so every such cover works. Neither its members nor its indexing family were replaced.

source.place: Second sentence, concluding local finite presentation on the same cover (and hence on the same strata when the parent applies this lemma).

proof_origin.place: Second sentence, expanded using the existing internal inverse-image comparison twice and the internal finite-presentation lemma; no coefficient-ring identification is needed.

Not in the drop list, no repair note, side-live item still unsplit, no SGA. It realizes the second sentence of main-20261015 lem-sfb-extend-subfield-constructible.proof.md ('tensoring a local finite presentation … on the same stratification'). Steps: (1) and (2) apply lem-sfb-internal-extension-inverse-image first to f with E_X→F_X, then to each cover member u_i with R=f^{-1}E_X and S=f^{-1}F_X; mapMod(u_i^*) of θ is an S_i-linear iso, and the rings match the u_i^*R in def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented, so no coefficient identification is hidden. (3) lem-sfb-internal-extension-finite-presentation applies on U_i without flatness, giving coker(a_{i,S}). (4) Elementary: the same cover, which was arbitrary, witnesses the conclusion. Edge cases E=F, f=id, empty Z, zero modules and infinite covers are fine; neither lemma needs qcqs. Same route as sibling lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible step 2. The overlap between lem-sfb-internal-scalar-extension-finite-presentation and the stronger lemma predates this delivery; the stronger one is cited. One repair: step 1 did not check that E_X and F_X are commutative, which the inverse-image lemma requires.
